text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- Parliament's local government and police committee Monday voted in favour of the appointment of Laszlo Forgacs as the new national police commander.

- Interior Minister Gabor Kuncze said on Monday that his ministry has repeatedly tried in the past two years to transform the organisation of the police force, but has experienced continued efforts on the part of National Police Headquarters to centralise power.
- President of the Hungarian Tax Authority Zoltan Pitti offered his resignation Monday, citing personal and family reasons. Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy accepted it.
- Parliament began a debate Monday on a bill which, if passed, would enable Hungarians to allocate one percent of their personal income tax for various public purposes from next year.

- Hungarian Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs asserted at the OSCE summit conference in Lisbon Monday that differences between Russia and the West regarding the expansion of NATO are no longer irreconcilable.
NEPSZABADSAG

- Citing unnamed sources, this paper reports that several MPs in the Socialist Party presidium have called for a special session on December 9, seeking an explanation from Premier Gyula Horn for recent personel changes within the cabinet.
- Defence Minister Gyorgy Keleti flew to Turkey on Monday for a two-day official visit.
- The State Privatisation and Holding Co. is considering offering a 12-18 percent stake in the Hungarian Oil and Gas company MOL for sale in February.
- A total of 10 Iraqis were expelled from Hungary as their status as political refugees had not been proven.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- Socialist parliamentary group leader Imre Szekeres said the next parliamentary elections could be held in May, 1998.

- Hungary has fallen back to fifth position in the list of attractive targets for capital investment in Central and Eastern Europe, says a study by experts of the American financial magazine Wall Street Journal Europe.
MAGYAR HIRLAP

- The official who will represent Hungary at the upcoming trial in the Hague concerning the controversial Gabcikovo hydroelectric power plant said that the trial may begin a few days later than the originally scheduled date of February 17, 1997.
- A total of HUF 10.5 billion has been spent on preparations for EU membership over the last three years, a report by the State Audit Office reveals.

- Hungary has good chances of improving its GDP by 2.5 percent next year and by a steady 5 percent in following years, said Michael Kevehazi, managing director of auditing and consultancy firm KPMG Hungaria.
- Konzum Kereskedelmi es Ipari Rt. is set to raise its equity through the exclusive issue of a share package worth HUF 826 million.
- The regional centre of Pepsi Cola International will move to Budapest from Vienna early next year.
MAGYAR NEMZET
- Vandals opened crypts, pushed tombstones over and scattered covering slabs at the Jewish cemetery in Szentgotthard.
-- Budapest newsroom (36-1) 327 4040
